indications: Indicated for the reduction of fever and treatment of mild to moderate pain (dysmenorrhea, headache, dental pain, migraine, post-operative pain) and inflammatory conditions including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.
dosage_and_administration: Adults for mild to moderate pain/fever: 200 mg to 400 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum single over-the-counter dose is 400 mg. Maximum daily dose for OTC self-medication is 1200 mg in 24 hours; prescription daily maximum under medical supervision is 2400 mg to 3200 mg per day divided into 3 or 4 doses. Must be taken with food or a glass of milk to reduce gastrointestinal irritation.
contraindications: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: Active peptic ulcer disease, history of recurrent gastrointestinal ulceration, bleeding, or perforation. Severe heart failure (NYHA Class IV), severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min), and severe hepatic failure. Patients with 'aspirin triad' (history of asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions precipitated by aspirin or other NSAIDs). Third trimester of pregnancy (causes premature closure of ductus arteriosus and fetal renal impairment).
drug_interactions: Co-administration with anticoagulants (Warfarin, Apixaban, Dabigatran) or antiplatelet agents (Aspirin, Clopidogrel) synergistically increases major GI bleeding risk. Concomitant use with SSRIs/SNRIs further multiplies gastrointestinal hemorrhage risk. Diminishes the antihypertensive effectiveness of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers, and diuretics. Increases serum Lithium, Methotrexate, and Digoxin concentrations to toxic levels. Concomitant use with Corticosteroids markedly elevates gastric ulceration risk.
side_effects: Common: Dyspepsia, nausea, abdominal pain, heartburn, diarrhea, dizziness, fluid retention, and mild peripheral edema. Serious: Peptic ulceration with hemorrhage or perforation, acute kidney injury (tubulointerstitial nephritis), hyperkalemia, myocardial infarction, stroke, and exacerbation of hypertension.
critical_warnings: CARDIOVASCULAR AND GASTROINTESTINAL BLACK BOX WARNING: NSAIDs cause an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, which can be fatal. NSAIDs also cause serious gastrointestinal adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines, which can occur at any time without warning symptoms. Elderly patients and patients with prior ulcer history are at highest risk.
